description: I’m building AstraVital, a prototype dashboard/kiosk for an astronaut’s daily health check-in. The prototype demonstrates how health information could support astronaut self-monitoring during a long mission.
summary: AstraVital is an offline, edge-computing crew health and care ecosystem engineered for long-duration deep-space transit to mitigate operational compliance fatigue and ensure 100% data autonomy during 20-minute communication blackouts. We developed a robust edge kiosk architecture featuring passive, microchip-embedded NFC smart cards for privacy-first, camera-free authentication, coupled with a deterministic Python backend (astravital_core.py) that evaluates 7-day predictive velocity decay, synchronizes check-ins to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), and compresses telemetry into encrypted 427-byte binary packets for secure store-and-forward queueing. This system directly addresses NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 habitability standards and Human Research Program (HRP-47065) medical risk guidelines by proactively tracking physiological parameters—such as mass loss and cardiovascular deconditioning—without imposing invasive clinical overhead or breaching astronaut privacy. It is critically important for deep-space exploration because it bridges the gap between complex aerospace power protection constraints and human-centric workflows, ensuring continuous protocol compliance and crew well-being across interplanetary missions to Mars and beyond.
details:
What it does and how it works:

AstraVital is an offline, edge-computing crew health and care ecosystem (CHCS) engineered to support astronauts during long-duration deep-space missions. The system operates entirely autonomously on onboard spacecraft single-board computers, ensuring zero reliance on continuous ground communication or cloud infrastructure. Astronauts authenticate locally by tapping a battery-free, microchip-embedded NFC smart card against an edge kiosk sensor pad. Once authenticated, the system’s deterministic Python backend (astravital_core.py) executes O(1) state lookups, logs daily check-ins synchronized to Coordinated Universal Time (06:00–10:00 UTC) to maintain operational discipline, and processes physiological metrics. It computes a 7-day predictive velocity decay model (flagging rapid mass drops exceeding 0.3 kg/day to proactively identify muscle atrophy and deconditioning. During orbital communication blackouts, health records are automatically compressed and encrypted into a 427-byte binary buffer for secure store-and-forward DSN telemetry queueing.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

AstraVital solves major deep-space operational challenges by eliminating compliance fatigue and privacy-invasive monitoring. By replacing camera-based surveillance with passive NFC badges, it safeguards astronaut psychological privacy while guaranteeing 100% operational resilience during 20-minute communication latencies. Its intended impact is to safeguard long-duration transit crews against physiological deconditioning, maintain high protocol compliance without imposing heavy clinical overhead, and provide mission controllers with reliable, compressed health intelligence that aligns directly with aerospace human factors requirements.

Tools, Languages, Hardware, and Software Used:

The project was developed using Python for core system logic, data processing, and binary telemetry compression, alongside HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interactive web dashboard deployed on GitHub Pages. Hardware considerations and electrical architecture encompass ARM-based edge single-board computer specifications, 28V DC spacecraft microgrid power protection topologies with Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) surge diodes, and passive NFC inductive sensor modules. PCB and structural layouts were conceptualized using KiCad and EasyEDA, housed within ruggedized anodized aluminum 6061-T6 chassis designs.

Creativity and Design Considerations:

AstraVital is creative because it rethinks crew monitoring through the lens of extreme privacy and hardware minimalism. Instead of relying on power-hungry, privacy-intrusive biometric cameras, it leverages battery-free NFC identification and edge-computed predictive health analytics. In designing the system, our team carefully considered aerospace constraints—such as power bus microgrid voltage fluctuations, DSN bandwidth limitations, zero-gravity usability, and strict compliance with human spaceflight standards including NASA-STD-3001 (Vol 2) for habitability and NASA HRP-47065 medical risk evidence reports—ensuring that every software and hardware layer is practical, scientifically rigorous, and ready for deep-space deployment.
